manifesto.statement: Most leaders do not need more advice. They need one room where nobody needs anything from them — and someone in it who will say the thing their team has stopped saying.

method.head:
HOW THE WORK RUNS

Four moves,

programs.head:
WAYS TO WORK TOGETHER

Three engagements.
No packages.

Every engagement starts with the same chemistry call and the same question: what would have to be different a year from now?

cards.title: The First Hundred Days
cards.desc: A focused engagement for the first quarter in a bigger seat: reading the board, resetting the team you inherited, and deciding what you will be known for.

cards.title: The Principal Year
cards.desc: The core engagement. We work on the three or four behaviours that decide how your team experiences you, and we measure them — before, midway and after.

cards.title: The Leadership Bench
cards.desc: Team coaching for the layer below the CEO: how you disagree, how you decide, and what happens in the room after the CEO leaves it.

results.title: Measured by the people around you.
results.subtitle: EVIDENCE

stats.label: AVERAGE SHIFT IN TEAM TRUST SCORE

cases.title: From the numbers person to the second voice in the room.
cases.story: Promoted from finance director eight months before an IPO process. We worked on presence with the board and on letting a strong team be strong.

cases.title: A founder who stopped being the bottleneck.
cases.story: Forty people, every decision through one inbox. A year later the exec team runs the week and the founder runs the next three years.

cases.title: Promoted twice in eighteen months.
cases.story: Technically brilliant, politically invisible. We built a way of being heard in rooms where the loudest voice usually won.

cases.title: Leading eleven thousand people through a merger.
cases.story: Two cultures, one winter. The work was about tempo: what to decide this week, what to refuse to decide, and how to say both out loud.

about.heading: Twenty years inside rooms like yours.
paragraphs: Before coaching I ran operations for a 900-person business and sat on two boards. I know what Monday morning feels like after a bad Friday board meeting — and I know most of it is fixable.

cards.title: The meeting after the meeting
cards.excerpt: If the real conversation happens in the corridor, your meeting is theatre. How to move the truth back into the room.

cards.title: Your first ninety days are not a plan
cards.excerpt: New CEOs arrive with a deck. The ones who last arrive with questions and a very short list of promises.

cards.title: Feedback travels upward slowly
cards.excerpt: The more senior you are, the older your information about yourself. A practical way to shorten the delay.

cards.title: Deciding what not to decide
cards.excerpt: Tempo is a leadership tool. Some decisions improve with a week; some rot. Telling them apart is the job.
